name: tutorial
notes: Thresholds marked TUNE are provisional until the Phase 4 test clip. Davis owns this file; agents propose changes.

edit.silence_policy_note: cut_all (user, 2026-10-29): every pause is cut, screen activity or not, unless the speaker announces a silent demo (range flagged keep_silence). keep_active = the original rule (active must_keep spans protected).
edit.air_note: air_ms: silence left at every join. compact_gap_ms: word-to-word pauses longer than this are cut down to air_ms. Intro = ranges whose beat starts with INTRO or whose source stem starts with 'intro'. Body 180 ms set by the user 2026-10-29 (v2 felt right for intro material; body a little slower). air_ms is only the fallback for clips without a loudness envelope.
edit.tail_note: User, 2026-10-29, after the first 1-hour run: no clipped word endings, ever. Every edge is placed on the clip's loudness envelope (silences.py writes E/silences/<stem>.envelope.json): sound = louder than the room floor + margin_db; a word has faded after hold_ms of quiet. tail_ms of air is left after the real fade and lead_ms before the real onset, so a join holds tail + lead (body 280 ms, intro 100 ms). An edge never extends past max_tail/max_lead or to within 40 ms of a word the range does not keep. Body tail 200 is the user's suggestion; it gets an A/B test.
edit.pacing_note: User, 2026-11-03, after claudesetup: the body felt sluggish; body join gap halved (tail 200->100, lead 80->40, so 140 ms per join; air 180->90; pauses over 175 ms cut, was 350). Intro unchanged.
edit.envelope_note: max_tail_ms 400 -> 800 (2026-11-03): 'approval' rang on 650 ms past its transcript end and the 400 ms cap chopped it. margin_db 12 -> 20 with the voice-band envelope (2026-11-03, user: body not punchy): the band-limited floor sits ~15 dB lower, so 12 dB let room echo count as speech. edge_margin_db 13 (2026-11-03): where a range's first/last word starts/ends uses this gentler line (soft final 's'), pauses still use margin_db. Envelope is high-pass only (sibilants kept).

render.voice_filter_note: User, 2026-11-05, picked from a blind-ish A/B (mictest_M3): MacBook mic, tone fix plus only a LIGHT denoise. 2-pole high-pass at 80 Hz, -4 dB at 220 Hz and -2 dB at 450 Hz (room boom/boxiness), +2.5 dB at 3.5 kHz (clarity), very light FFT denoise (nr 6: stronger settings made the voice sound robotic/warbly), gentle 2.5:1 compression. The denoiser delays audio ~25 ms; render_tutorial measures and cancels that. Replaces the 2026-11-03 chain (4-pole 100 Hz, -5 dB 220 Hz, +3 dB 3.5 kHz, afftdn nr 10, 3:1). Set to "" to turn off.

output.note: User, 2026-11-19 (Rio 1 for OBS recordings): every video comes out 16:9 4K HEVC so YouTube streams it at its 4K bitrate. A 1080p recording is scaled up 2x (lanczos), a non-16:9 one gets black bars, never stretched. quality = hevc_videotoolbox constant quality (Rio 2.0 uses 80; 85 is higher). size null = the recording's own size, libx264 CRF 20 (the old Rio). prio_speed: the encoder's speed switch, 1.86x faster at 4K60 on the M3 with the same picture (SSIM 0.9997 vs without, same file size; 2026-11-19 bench).

budget.token_budget_note: Pro window size isn't published. Leave null (warn only) until Phase 4 measurements set it.

estimator_priors.notes: Rough starting guesses; replaced by history medians after the first runs.
estimator_priors.scribe_usd_note: Now AssemblyAI (2026-10-29). Third-party listings: Universal-2 about $0.15/h, Universal-3 Pro about $0.21/h. Confirm against the user's real bill.
estimator_priors.render4k_note: 2026-11-19 bench: 108 s of 1080p60 OBS-style video rendered to 4K HEVC q85 + prio_speed in 78.4 s (= 1.46 s per 1000 output-frame megapixels; ~43 s per output minute at 60 fps, ~22 at 30), peak 350 MB. blur: Rio 2.0 drive-organizer trial, 475 s for a 21-min edit at 1 s steps, 410 MB.

blur.note: User, 2026-11-17 (Rio 2.0) and 2026-11-19 (Rio 1): blur emails, phone numbers, API keys, IDs, KEY=value lines, an open Gmail pane and the whole screen inside a private folder automatically (blur_find.py --sensitive), every 1 s. Careful: only clearly sensitive text, never random words. Skipped when the user answers 'no' to 'Any sensitive info on screen?' (E/sensitive.json).
